### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Among the given options, primary aldosteronism (Conn Syndrome) is the most plausible condition to cause hypermagnesemia. This condition involves excess aldosterone, which can lead to compensatory magnesium retention. Other conditions like hyperparathyroidism, diabetes mellitus, and kwashiorkor are more commonly associated with hypomagnesemia or do not directly affect magnesium levels to cause hypermagnesemia.
